comment: Season formats, from the brief. season.js runs these; nothing about the formats lives in code.
_leagues: Bottom to top. The player starts in the first.
_cycle: Two league seasons, then a Giant Nut season, then round again.

league._groupStage: Round robin inside each group: 4 fights each.

finals._seeding: Group winners seed 1-6 by record, runners-up 7-12, wild cards 13-16.

league._movement: The top 4 of the final ranking go up a league, the bottom 4 down. The final ranking is how far a robot got in the finals, then its group record.

giantNut._bracket: 60 qualifiers in a 64 bracket seeded by group performance; the top 4 seeds get first-round byes.
giantNut._effect: None on the leagues: every robot goes back to the league it was in.

evolution._comment: The off-season (js/logic/evolution.js): every AI team works on its robot between seasons. Budget is per season by league plus perWin, saved if not spent; upgrades are real parts, bought only if the team's tests (fast resolver, fixed seeds, both corners, against evalOpponents robots from its league) show at least minGain more wins. A robot under belowWinShare for worstSeasons seasons running may be redesigned around a new weapon (front-weapon bodies only).

rating._rating: Each driver learns toward a ceiling `talent` above their starting rating, `learn` of the way each season; a season's results (win share - 0.5) x perWinShare and noise move them about it.

cup._comment: Tournament mode (js/logic/cup.js): one-off tournaments outside the career. `groupSize` and `advance` are the groups format's; the Giant Nut format uses `giantNut` above. Robots are repaired between fights. Up to `maxPlayers` people can enter, each with a robot.

formats.name: Knockout
formats.blurb: One bracket, seeded by driver rating. Lose once and you are out.

formats.name: Groups, then knockout
formats.blurb: Groups of four fight a round robin; the top two of each go into a seeded bracket.

formats.name: The Giant Nut
formats.blurb: All 120 robots: ten groups of twelve, eight fights each, then a 64-robot bracket.

rivalry._comment: Robots with a history against the player (js/logic/rivalry.js). Every meeting adds heat - more for the things fans remember - and heat cools between seasons (`decay` is what is kept). `levels` is the heat for a rivalry, a bitter rivalry and a nemesis. A rival tests `prepOptions` more setups against you per level (only at a difficulty where opponents test at all) and drives `skillPerLevel` sharper; promoters pay `gatePerLevel` of the appearance fee per level. A win over a robot `upsetTiers` leagues above you (or a loss to one below) is an upset. Grudge matches pay the bigger league's purses times the `grudge` factors, `perLevel` more for a hotter rivalry.
